$comment: Shared table for the XML prologue declaration inspector. Go (InspectXMLPrologue) and TypeScript (inspectXmlPrologue) both read it, so neither language can drift. The three facts are reported separately because they are three different attack surfaces and the POLICY over them belongs to the consumer, not here: an external identifier is the XXE/SSRF vector, an inline entity is the billion-laughs vector, and a subset of only ELEMENT/ATTLIST/NOTATION is inert. When leadingCommentBytes > 0 the suite prepends a comment of that many filler bytes before `xml`, which is how the cases that used to defeat the 4 KB scan window are expressed without embedding 4 KB of literal text here. `malformed` is true when the prologue could not be parsed to a root element: the other facts are then a lower bound, and a boundary that treats absence of findings as safe must refuse the input instead of accepting it.

cases.name: plain document
cases.why: no prologue declaration of either kind

cases.name: empty input
cases.why: nothing to scan; must not panic or index out of range

cases.name: whitespace only
cases.why: no root element is ever reached

cases.name: doctype first
cases.why: an external DTD reference needs no inline ENTITY to be an XXE vector

cases.name: doctype after the xml declaration
cases.why: the declaration is skipped, the DOCTYPE is still in the prologue

cases.name: doctype lowercase
cases.why: XML keywords are case-sensitive but scanners must not be fooled by case

cases.name: doctype with an internal subset declaring an entity
cases.why: the billion-laughs shape; both detectors fire

cases.name: doctype beyond the legacy 4 KB scan window
cases.why: THE BUG: a fixed 4 KB window accepts this. The prologue has no length bound, so neither may the scan

cases.name: entity beyond the legacy 4 KB scan window
cases.why: the same bug in the entity detector itself, which is what the converters gate on

cases.name: doctype-shaped text in character data
cases.xml: <note><!DOCTYPE fake> and a literal <!DOCTYPE never here</note>
cases.why: scanning stops at the root element, so content cannot false-positive

cases.name: doctype-shaped text in an attribute value
cases.why: the root element is reached first; its attributes are not prologue

cases.name: entity-shaped text after the root element
cases.why: an ENTITY past the root cannot be a declaration, so flagging it would reject valid documents

cases.name: doctype-shaped text inside a prologue comment
cases.why: a commented declaration is not a declaration; the comment is skipped as a unit

cases.name: unterminated prologue comment
cases.why: no root element is reachable, so there is no prologue to have declared anything; must terminate, not loop

cases.name: processing instruction before the doctype
cases.why: any number of PIs may precede the DOCTYPE

cases.name: doctype with an inert internal subset
cases.why: real Burp Suite export shape: declares structure only, so it can neither expand nor fetch

cases.name: doctype with a PUBLIC external identifier
cases.why: an external DTD is an XXE/SSRF vector with no inline ENTITY of its own

cases.name: doctype with a SYSTEM external identifier and an entity
cases.why: both vectors at once; the classic file-disclosure payload

cases.name: external-identifier keyword in an inert subset comment
cases.xml: <!DOCTYPE n [<!-- SYSTEM is only a word here --><!ELEMENT n EMPTY>]><n/>
cases.why: the keyword must be recognised as a declaration token, not by substring search

cases.name: entity hidden behind a quoted ]> in an ATTLIST default
cases.why: GATE BYPASS: ]> inside a quoted literal is not the end of the subset. A scanner that searches for the first ]> loses its place and reports a clean document

cases.name: entity hidden behind a ]> in a subset comment
cases.why: same evasion through a comment rather than a quoted literal

cases.name: notation with an external identifier inside the subset
cases.why: an external reference can live INSIDE the subset, where a check that only inspects the DOCTYPE's own external-id position cannot see it

cases.name: single-quoted ]> in an entity value
cases.why: both quote characters delimit literals in a DTD, not just the double quote
